newsitem.title: USA: S. Africa central banker says rates steady for now.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa central banker says rates steady for now.

text.p: South Africa Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said Tuesday the central bank would not lower interest rates unless it sees improvement in the current account, and would hike rates unless the figures improved.

"We are not going to create liquidity at this stage and not going to try to bring interest rates down until we see some adjustment taking place in the imports and current accounts," Stals told reporters here.
Stals added that he felt confident that South Africa would be able to reduce its trade deficit because of a weaker rand, and lower liquidity in the banking sector.
He expressed confidence that developments in the business cycle and tighter monetary policy would force adjustment in the current accounts and the balance of payments.

"Our decision for the time being is to maintain the status quo," Stals said. "If we dont get the right signal soon that the economy is mnoving in the right direction, the next step will be to tighten monetary policy.
He also said that he would have no problem going to the International Monetary Fund at any time for funds to stabilize the eocnomy, but that the country's first line of defense was its reserves.
He said that a recent IMF report warning the country against rapid lifting of currency controls confirmed the long held views of the cnetral bank.
"We dont like exchange controls, we would like to get rid of exchange controls," he said, explaining that the central bank hoped for the eventual elimination of the controls.
"There is no time frame (for full liberalization)," he said. "It depends on foreign reserve positions, capital inflows, current account positions and so on."
South Africa might need to grow accustomed to the kind of rapid capital movements witnessed on international markets, Stals said.

"Countries must learn to live with the world of volatile capital inflows and outflows," he said adding "But it makes it extremely difficult ot lean against the wind, to maintain financial stability, if you don't have any foreign reserves."
